=== Row Yaniv ===

DECK: 54 cards, used only for their values: 2 Jokers worth 0; 4 each of values 1 to 9 (Ace = 1); 16 cards worth 10 (10s, Jacks, Queens, Kings). Suits are ignored.

STATE: You have 3 private slots c1, c2, c3; each holds one card value or is empty (-1). Your hand total H is the sum of your non-empty slots. Penalty totals are public and start at 0. The table shows the round (1 to 24), the priority seat (seat 1 in round 1), the draw pile size (its order is hidden), the OFFER ROW (an ordered public list of cards) and the DEAD PILE (every card that has left play this hand).

EACH ROUND:
1. NEW HAND. If a new hand is due: all 54 cards are shuffled into the draw pile, all slots and the dead pile are emptied, each player in seat order is dealt 3 cards into c1, c2, c3 (told privately), and the next card is turned face up as the offer row (1 card at position 1).
2. The offer row with positions, the dead pile, the draw pile size, the priority seat and everyone's card count are announced.
3. CHOICES. Everyone answers at the same moment, privately: (a) action: YANIV, DRAW or TAKE; (b) take position: 1 to the length of the offer row (used only for TAKE); (c) shed slot: 1, 2 or 3. If your chosen shed slot is empty, your lowest-numbered non-empty slot is used instead.
4. YANIV CHECK. A YANIV is valid only if your H is 10 or less. If it is valid you are a caller. If it is not, it is announced as invalid and you are treated as DRAW for the rest of the round.
5. If at least one valid YANIV was made, no cards move this round and a showdown follows (go to step 10). If none was made, steps 6 to 9 happen.
6. SHED. Each player removes the card in their shed slot, and every other slot of theirs holding the same value is also removed (a pair sheds two cards, a triple three). Those extra slots stay empty for the rest of the hand. Every player's shed values are announced.
7. TAKE. TAKE players are resolved in seat order starting at the priority seat and wrapping around. Each receives the offer-row card at their take position if no earlier player has claimed it, and places it in their shed slot; who took which card is announced. If the card was already claimed, that player becomes DRAW instead.
8. DRAW. In the same order, each DRAW player takes the top card of the draw pile into their shed slot, told only to them; the drawn value is never announced and the draw pile shrinks by 1 per draw.
9. ROW UPDATE. Offer-row cards not taken go to the dead pile. The new offer row is every card shed in step 6, in seat order from seat 1, and in slot order within a player. Card counts and the draw pile size are announced.
10. SHOWDOWN happens if a valid YANIV was made this round, or the draw pile holds fewer cards than there are players after step 9, or this is round 24. All hands are revealed. With valid callers: M is the lowest H among callers, N the lowest H among non-callers (N = 99 if everyone called). A caller scores 0 if their H equals M and M is less than N; otherwise they score H + 20 (Asaf). A non-caller scores 0 if their H is less than or equal to M; otherwise they score H. With no valid caller: every player with the lowest H scores 0 and the others score their H. Scores are added to penalty totals, all totals are announced, and the next round begins a fresh hand and a fresh shuffle. Without a showdown the hand continues next round.
11. The priority seat passes to the next seat, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1.
12. END. The match ends after any showdown that leaves some penalty total at 50 or more, or after round 24; otherwise play continues.

There is no discussion. When the match ends, the lowest penalty total wins; players tied for the lowest share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

  shed_slot    answer with a whole number, in the range you are given

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
DECK: 54 cards, used only for their values: 2 Jokers worth 0; 4 each of values 1 to 9 (Ace = 1); 16 cards worth 10 (10s, Jacks, Queens, Kings). Suits are ignored.

STATE: You have 3 private slots c1, c2, c3; each holds one card value or is empty (-1). Your hand total H is the sum of your non-empty slots. Penalty totals are public and start at 0. The table shows the round (1 to 24), the priority seat (seat 1 in round 1), the draw pile size (its order is hidden), the OFFER ROW (an ordered public list of cards) and the DEAD PILE (every card that has left play this hand).

EACH ROUND:
1. NEW HAND. If a new hand is due: all 54 cards are shuffled into the draw pile, all slots and the dead pile are emptied, each player in seat order is dealt 3 cards into c1, c2, c3 (told privately), and the next card is turned face up as the offer row (1 card at position 1).
2. The offer row with positions, the dead pile, the draw pile size, the priority seat and everyone's card count are announced.
3. CHOICES. Everyone answers at the same moment, privately: (a) action: YANIV, DRAW or TAKE; (b) take position: 1 to the length of the offer row (used only for TAKE); (c) shed slot: 1, 2 or 3. If your chosen shed slot is empty, your lowest-numbered non-empty slot is used instead.
4. YANIV CHECK. A YANIV is valid only if your H is 10 or less. If it is valid you are a caller. If it is not, it is announced as invalid and you are treated as DRAW for the rest of the round.
5. If at least one valid YANIV was made, no cards move this round and a showdown follows (go to step 10). If none was made, steps 6 to 9 happen.
6. SHED. Each player removes the card in their shed slot, and every other slot of theirs holding the same value is also removed (a pair sheds two cards, a triple three). Those extra slots stay empty for the rest of the hand. Every player's shed values are announced.
7. TAKE. TAKE players are resolved in seat order starting at the priority seat and wrapping around. Each receives the offer-row card at their take position if no earlier player has claimed it, and places it in their shed slot; who took which card is announced. If the card was already claimed, that player becomes DRAW instead.
8. DRAW. In the same order, each DRAW player takes the top card of the draw pile into their shed slot, told only to them; the drawn value is never announced and the draw pile shrinks by 1 per draw.
9. ROW UPDATE. Offer-row cards not taken go to the dead pile. The new offer row is every card shed in step 6, in seat order from seat 1, and in slot order within a player. Card counts and the draw pile size are announced.
10. SHOWDOWN happens if a valid YANIV was made this round, or the draw pile holds fewer cards than there are players after step 9, or this is round 24. All hands are revealed. With valid callers: M is the lowest H among callers, N the lowest H among non-callers (N = 99 if everyone called). A caller scores 0 if their H equals M and M is less than N; otherwise they score H + 20 (Asaf). A non-caller scores 0 if their H is less than or equal to M; otherwise they score H. With no valid caller: every player with the lowest H scores 0 and the others score their H. Scores are added to penalty totals, all totals are announced, and the next round begins a fresh hand and a fresh shuffle. Without a showdown the hand continues next round.
11. The priority seat passes to the next seat, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1.
12. END. The match ends after any showdown that leaves some penalty total at 50 or more, or after round 24; otherwise play continues.

There is no discussion. When the match ends, the lowest penalty total wins; players tied for the lowest share the win.
